caption: When Jesus says Moses wrote about him, does he mean Deuteronomy’s prophet? It is plausible, but John never names the passage—and Deuteronomy’s meaning is disputed.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Which words of Moses? Jesus says Moses wrote about him. Christians often identify the promised prophet in Deuteronomy as one of those passages.
slides.body: Jesus says Moses wrote about him. Christians often identify the promised prophet in Deuteronomy as one of those passages.
slides.heading: Which words of Moses?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Deut 18:15-16: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers.
slides.body: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers.
slides.heading: Deut 18:15-16

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Jn 5:45–47, BSB: If you had believed Moses, you would believe Me, because he wrote about Me.
slides.body: If you had believed Moses, you would believe Me, because he wrote about Me.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Jn 5:45–47

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Why this passage is plausible It promises a prophet like Moses, and Acts later quotes that promise while preaching about Jesus.
slides.body: It promises a prophet like Moses, and Acts later quotes that promise while preaching about Jesus.
slides.heading: Why this passage is plausible

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But John never names it Jesus may mean the Torah more broadly. Deuteronomy may also describe a line of prophets rather than one final person.
slides.body: Jesus may mean the Torah more broadly. Deuteronomy may also describe a line of prophets rather than one final person.

title: Moses wrote about me
